minutes.headline: Select Board voted 2-1 with two abstentions to recommend against the water district's PFAS treatment plan on the May 16 ballot.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a water district presentation on PFAS treatment and redundancy, followed by a presentation from Lunenburg Citizens for Affordable Clean Water opposing the plan. The board first rejected a motion to take no position, then voted to recommend disapproval. It also approved a letter supporting the governor's senior tax exemption amendment, signed warrants, skipped remaining items and adjourned because the building lights shut off.

public_comment.topic: Board of Health lost a member and needs write-in candidates for the open ballot seat to keep a quorum.
Criticised cemetery commission and proposed a cemetery corporation; asked to be on next week's agenda.
Resident asked that the room's audio be improved so people can hear presenters and the board.
Resident said the water commissioners could not be heard with their backs to the audience.
Asked whether the 32.2 million vote is what must be done for PFAS and whether SRF funding is approved.
Asked about an emergency plan if the Keating well failed and how much the project would cost the town's buildings.

public_comment.topic: Presented opposition to the water district plan; urged the board to support a no vote.

budget_items.topic: State revolving fund loan for PFAS treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: The district said it received a state letter finding the added Lancaster Ave scope eligible for SRF financing; board members questioned whether funding is actually approved.
The district gave a per-quarter cost per customer assuming principal forgiveness.
The district showed the minimum charge and usage rate rising sharply, compared against sewer rates.
Board member questioned whether the loan is 20 or 30 years and how compounding affects interest; district said 30 years is available on request.
District said the warrant article appropriates the full amount so the loan process is not delayed.
The consultant estimated annual media replacement costs with heavy caveats; board members noted operating costs were not presented.
The citizens group argued the full plan costs far more than treating only Keating and Lancaster.
A resident cited cemetery fund balances and the cost of forming a cemetery corporation.
The chair read accounts payable and payroll warrants.

decisions.decision: Chair said the investigation report may not be reached; he will send the draft to members and ask the town manager to post it for next week.
Water commissioners were asked to face the audience and the table was rearranged so the room could hear.
Board concluded it had voted not to endorse the water district's plan as presented.
Remaining agenda items and board comments were skipped because the building lights shut off.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 2-1, with two abstentions, to recommend against the water district's PFAS treatment plan on the May 16 ballot.
A motion to take no action and make no recommendation either way had failed first.
The board approved a letter supporting the governor's amendment to the means-tested senior citizen property tax exemption.
Most of the meeting was a water district presentation on the plan's cost, rates and loan, followed by a presentation from a citizens group opposing it.
The remaining agenda items and board comments were skipped when the building lights shut off.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked to vote on the water district's PFAS project on the May 16 ballot, and the Select Board's recommendation is a no.

Board members and residents questioned whether the state revolving fund financing is actually approved and noted that operating costs were not presented, so the full effect on water rates is not settled in the record.
watch_next: The May 16 ballot vote on the water district's PFAS treatment project.
The chair's draft investigation report, which he said he would send to members and ask the town manager to post for next week.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the three non-procedural votes and on who was on the board. They differ on the vote tallies, one date on the ballot, the warrant figures (caption errors), and a long list of water-district and cemetery items that appear only in our minutes. The one thing to know: the official minutes give the PFAS "no recommendation" motion as failed 2-3-0, but ours records only that it failed; and our minutes show the meeting ending early when the lights shut off, which the official minutes do not mention.
